title: Leek, mushroom and butter bean hash with eggs

grandparents_cupboard.reason: Leeks, mushrooms, tinned butter beans, kale, eggs, cheddar, butter and oil are all ordinary home staples.

supermarket.reason: Every ingredient is an everyday item at any mainstream supermarket.

basic_kitchen.reason: It needs only a large lidded frying pan and a grater, with simple frying and eggs cooked in hollows.

works.reason: Three leeks, 250g mushrooms, two tins of beans, 100g kale and four eggs make a sensible hash for four, and the covered 4 minutes will set the whites.

honest_times.reason: Ten minutes is believable for slicing the leeks and mushrooms, with the kale and beans readied while they fry, and the 8+3+4 minutes in the steps match the 15 cook minutes.

honest_ingredients.reason: Every listed ingredient and seasoning is used, though step 2 says 'paprika' where the list says smoked paprika, which could be tightened.

seasonal_feel.reason: A hot leek-led hash with kale suits a cold January morning, and leeks are the base of the dish.

plain_voice.reason: The steps are clear, plain British English with no restaurant language.

hearty_healthy.reason: Vegetables, beans and eggs make a filling, balanced breakfast a family would happily repeat.
